chunk_map.heading: # Prove the bug, then ship the fix (title/lede)
Write the failing test and fix the root cause
Read the diff and push back on a line
Interrogate the fix for a deeper layer
There is always a next plausible answer

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5/L20/L22 'the bug you brought from prework' / 'Drop your bug after the colon' / {{prompt:fix-tests-first-1}} resolve under the session-artifact carve-out (student's own prework bug). L27 'the compound step reads this scrollback' resolves under the module-arc carve-out: getting-going.md's own 'What You'll Learn' names '**Compound** the session into a personal rules file' and Key Concepts states 'The loop is orient → fix → close → compound' — module include-order prior context. 'the agent' (first used L18, blockquote, chunk 1) is established before every later chunk that reuses it (L26, L31, L49).

Only cross-file reference is L5 'the bug you brought from prework' — named by title ('prework'), not located by position; passes the navigational-pointer carve-out. No 'the opening lecture said…'-style positional callback anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L5 'the bug you brought from prework' — prework.md line 120-121 confirms 'Chosen trivial bug' is a prework artifact consumed by 'M1 fix-tests-first'. getting-going.md line 46 lists this exercise's include order directly after prework/orient-and-introspect, matching the backing block's 'Picks up from: orient-and-introspect'. Beat exists.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or instruction (chunk 4 closest to the shape: 'There will be a next plausible answer... A passing test you trust is what makes a layer real; when to stop digging is your call.' — a full claim, not a wait-state fragment). No chunk is a bare context-dependent bullet.

Each header is literally true of its chunk content: 'Write the failing test and fix the root cause' (chunk 1 body does exactly that); 'Read the diff and push back on a line' (chunk 2); 'Interrogate the fix for a deeper layer' (chunk 3); 'There is always a next plausible answer' (chunk 4 body: 'There will be a next plausible answer'); 'Ship the PR' (chunk 5: commit/push/open PR). Closest-to-violating candidate: chunk 4's declaration header, but body states it literally with no strengthening ('There will be a next plausible answer' — matches header verbatim in force).

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (L9 'pushing back is core work' is a claim about the exercise, not a graded superlative about itself — no 'one of the most useful moves' shape anywhere); no number-with-retraction (no numbers in body); no abstraction-noun stack; no empty-leg verb triplet. Closest candidate checked: L26 'The agent yields if you push hard enough, so its agreement settles nothing.' — single declarative, not a triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L33 'name what's still surface' uses 'surface' as an ordinary adjective/predicate (surface-level), not the banned noun sense ('writing surface'). 'scrollback' (L27) is ordinary terminal vocabulary, not repo-internal jargon. No 'compendium', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'mood', or 'Connections'-as-proper-noun anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 carries two bold spans (the L15 handle 'Tests-first, root-cause-driven.' and the L18 blockquote handle 'Small fix, small test.'), which is at or over the ≤1-per-slide budget on a literal count, but the maintainer block's dated accept-note (L60, 'Emphasis pass 2026-07-09, Antti-directed go very lightly on the bold') explicitly attests this exact configuration against check_slides.md §9 — 'Widget chrome... and the blockquote callout untouched'. Documented accept-note; not re-flagged. All other chunks carry zero or one bold handle (widget-chrome labels 'Optional.' etc. exempt per the same note).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: getting-going.md L46 links this file as a standard exercise include ('[Prove the bug, then ship the fix](exercises/fix-tests-first.md)'); exercise files render under the renderer's `.phase--exercise` wrapper by convention, so the whole body reaches the composed deck. No phase-less prose section in this file (every line is either title/lede or under a `##`), so there is no section at risk of the phase-less-drop failure mode rule 10 names.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/fix-tests-first.md` → 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' L20 'Drop your bug after the colon' points at the prompt block on L22, same `##` chunk — passes the same-chunk carve-out. L31 'a layer above it' is a conceptual (root-cause-vs-surface), not a page-position, reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/fix-tests-first.md` → 'files: 1  slides: 5  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets  oversized: 0 — ✓ every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four headings are imperative/phase-label as required for an exercise ('Write the failing test and fix the root cause', 'Read the diff and push back on a line', 'Interrogate the fix for a deeper layer', 'Ship the PR'). L43 'There is always a next plausible answer' is declarative, but this is the compendium's own named calibration specimen (rule 15's body: 'fix-tests-first.md — There is always a next plausible answer... at the moment its exercise generalises past its own task') and carries the maintainer's dated accept-note (L62): the deliberate one non-imperative heading in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No doctrine restatement (each bullet does new work, no re-announced split/lens/law), no aphorism kicker. Closest candidate: L27 'Your own wording matters. No pre-made prompt: the compound step reads this scrollback, so your push-back is what becomes a rule.' reads as self-referential design commentary (class b), but the maintainer block's dated accept-note (L56) explicitly reviewed and kept exactly this bullet ('Carded and kept, then trimmed... is the wanted motivation for authentic wording, not a leak — do not cut it as a pre-announcement'). Documented accept-note; not re-flagged.
